c0-frame.title: Frame the cycle
c0-frame.imperative: Set the cycle flavor (shotgun | compare | refine) in the top-level flavor field; the human picks, you may recommend. Refine: harden one direction, chase open threads, test load-bearing assumptions, tighten interfaces in deep-module terms. Record pass when framed.
c0-frame.finding: flavor=refine, human-set agenda: the degree question (how much of the mapping job goes procedural) via 4 named sub-questions + scip-python-on-f1Brainz excursion

q1.title: Kill condition: what would make this pointless?
q1.imperative: The parent never named a kill condition for this descendant. Ask the human what fact, if true, would mean the code map shouldn't be built. Record the answer as the finding.
q1.finding: Human: map usefulness already proven; kill condition = cannot replace the LLM-heavy Cartographer algorithmically AT ALL ('more or less dead'), but suspected to be a question of DEGREE, not true/false

q2.title: What does 'replace the Cartographer' mean concretely?
q2.imperative: Does the derived map need to reproduce the existing docs/architecture artifact set (index/packets/overlays in that format), or does it replace the map's FUNCTION with a new surface that downstream roles would consume differently? This sets the comparison criteria x1 measures against. Ask the human with a recommended answer; record the finding.
q2.finding: Human: replace the FUNCTION, not the artifact format; loss accounting is part of the job. Overlay dispositions: capabilities = really a why; decisions = arguably history, maybe retire to git history; constraints = listed IN the function as comments (assumption change -> code change -> comment change -> graph update). Code IS truth; algorithms project it into an interpretable graph

x1.title: Excursion: scip-python on f1Brainz — degree-of-coverage measurement
x1.imperative: One named question: how much of f1Brainz's existing Cartographer map can scip-python's output procedurally reproduce, and what does it structurally miss? Brief at excursions/x1-brief.md, recorded before dispatch. Background dispatch via run_crew.py registry (backend external) + Agent subagent. Result lands at excursions/x1-result.md and on the board before consolidation. Record the scoped verdict as the finding.
x1.finding: POSITIVE with sharp boundary. Runs in ~15min after 1-line Windows patch (0.6.6 broken on Windows; also silent-empty-index trap on forward-slash cwd — pipeline needs non-empty assertion). Index: 443 files, 3686 functions, 600 classes, 16767 named containers, 220915 occurrences. Degree split vs curated map (7793 lines): ~7% procedurally reproducible / ~50% skeleton-derivable-prose-judgment / ~43% untouchable (decisions, capabilities, why). Structural spine 100% reproducible: 34/34 curated dep edges confirmed, 0 missed, +5 real edges the map omits (drift found free). CRITICAL: scip-python emits ZERO WriteAccess — read/write distinction NOT available from SCIP, needs plain AST pass (Store/Load). Docstrings: ~72% classes/public functions seeded; containers nearly bare (4.1% fields). NOT tested: incrementality (load-bearing), rename identity, C++, second codebase. Full: excursions/x1-result.md

x2.title: Excursion: prior art on deriving a comment/concept layer alongside the structural layer
x2.imperative: One named question: has anyone built a system that derives a concept/comment layer TOGETHER WITH the variable/function structural layer, and what did they learn? Brief at excursions/x2-brief.md, recorded before dispatch. Background dispatch via run_crew.py registry (backend external) + Agent subagent. Result lands at excursions/x2-result.md and on the board before consolidation. Record the scoped verdict as the finding.
x2.finding: Prior art EXISTS: RepoDoc (2026) builds one graph with code+concept+doc nodes; its procedural/judgment split matches everyone else's — structure/diff/traversal procedural, concept naming+prose judgment. Best generator covers only ~53% of API (x5 measured the same hole from the harvest side). Reflexion models (1995): concept layer is an INPUT, derived part is the agreement/disagreement with structure. Doxygen grouping = 20-year-old answer to level mismatch (one concept spanning N declarations, stored in source). Write-back split 3 ways (into source / beside with git hook / never touch + re-anchor); org-babel lesson: write-back works iff emitted text carries provenance markers. Hole prioritization: real literature; centrality-vs-text contradiction carried unresolved. Full: excursions/x2-result.md

q3.title: Do constraint-bearing comments need a parseable convention, or stay free prose?
q3.imperative: Constraints/assumptions living in comments makes comments a semi-structured store the crawler reads. Ask: does the comment need a light convention (tagged fields the deterministic pipeline can classify) or stay free prose (whole comment = concept prose, classification left to the agent-assisted layer)? Recommend an answer; record the finding.
q3.finding: Human: prefix conventions expected for the comment-layer graph — easy, straightforward. Every comment is an ASSERTION (assumption / requirement / explanation); categorize and put into the graph. Assumes prior art exists for comment categorization (-> x3)

x3.title: Excursion: prior art on classifying code comments as typed assertions
x3.imperative: One named question: what taxonomies/tools exist for classifying code comments by assertion type (assumption, requirement, explanation, TODO, ...), and has anyone mapped classified comments into a knowledge graph? Brief at excursions/x3-brief.md. Background dispatch via registry + Agent subagent; result at excursions/x3-result.md. Record the scoped verdict as the finding.
x3.finding: Premise splits, opposite verdicts. (1) 'Every comment is an assertion' — genuine GAP: no study applies speech-act/assertion typing to code comments (published taxonomies classify by topic, not illocutionary force). (2) 'Easily categorize' — FALSE for the interesting classes as free-prose classification (NLBSE benchmark: rationale F1 0.21-0.31, dev-notes 0.33; easy classes are ones with explicit syntactic markers, F1 0.85-1.0) but TRUE one-kind-at-a-time as binary+template (assumptions F1 0.96 fine-tuned; trigger-action 0.79; iComment 90%+ in-project; Jdoctor 92%p/83%r). Rationale comments are only 2-4% of comments in two independent corpora. (3) comment->typed-statement->graph: NOT found anywhere (GraphGen4Code stores docstrings untyped). Design lean: prefix conventions at write time make comments self-classifying (the marker IS why easy classes are easy); hard numbers apply to legacy backfill, where per-kind binary extractors work. Full: excursions/x3-result.md

q4.title: Framing: developer-ergonomics standard, not invention
q4.imperative: Record the human's reframe: the code map = making life easy on agents the way good tooling/docs make life easy on developers; invent nothing new; define a constellation-skills standard over existing tools/conventions and teach local dev agents to use the artifacts. Record as finding.
q4.finding: Human: 'all im really doing here is making life easy on agents the same way we should make life easy on developers generally... we dont need to invent anything new, we can just create a standard for our constellation skills project and make sure the local constellation skills development agents know how to use the artifacts we're providing.' Deliverable shape becomes: adopt existing tools (extraction), define conventions (comment prefixes/grouping), produce artifacts, teach agents to consume them

x4.title: Excursion: hole-prioritization dry run on f1Brainz (centrality x docstring holes vs curated map)
x4.imperative: One named question: does centrality over the derived graph, intersected with docstring holes, reproduce the curated map's documentation choices on f1Brainz — and produce a credible describe-these-first list? Brief at excursions/x4-brief.md; result at excursions/x4-result.md. Record the scoped verdict as the finding.
x4.finding: NO for the planned signal, YES for a dumber one. PageRank over the symbol call graph fails to beat random at every K (lift 0.87-1.73x, p>=0.17; 50% of its top-30 are private helpers like _json_ready — propagation manufactures importance for beneath-notice utilities). HITS degenerate on this sparse near-acyclic graph. What VALIDATED: raw call frequency into public entities — top-10 60% map-named vs 19.4% base (p=0.005), top-30 47% (p=0.0005). Module-level test uninformative by construction (map names 95.2% of modules — ceiling). FREE TARGET: 130 of 487 map-named entities (27%) have no docstring — pre-certified worth-describing, no ranking signal needed. Artifact shipped: evidence/x4/hole_priority_list.md (692 public holes ordered by validated signal). f1Brainz coverage 62.3% (interrogate). NOT tested: betweenness, boundary-crossing, churn, text ranking, other repos (n=1). Full: excursions/x4-result.md

q5.imperative: Record the human's ruling on the C++ arm's weight. Record as finding.
